question: Which languages do live caption apps for deaf people support?
slides: Captions in *60 languages,* on your phone.
description: Captio AI, a live captions app for deaf and hard of hearing people, captions and translates speech in 60 languages, from English, Spanish and Chinese to Welsh and Basque.
Captio AI is made for deaf and hard of hearing people, so the language someone speaks does not decide whether you can follow the conversation.
The World Health Organization says over 430 million people need rehabilitation for disabling hearing loss, and projects nearly 2.5 billion will have some hearing loss by 2050.
Captio AI has a page for each of its 60 languages that lists the regional varieties it supports, for example British, American and Australian English.
Captio AI keeps captioning when a speaker changes language in the middle of a sentence, and a language hint lets you name the language you expect.
Live Translator in Captio AI puts the translation beside the original captions, so you read both as the person talks.
The home page, the four feature pages and the organizations page of the Captio AI website exist in all 60 languages, through the language menu.
The free plan of Captio AI includes 100 free credits a day, and the app costs nothing to download on iPhone and Android.
Captio AI needs internet for live captions and translation, its output can contain mistakes, and it does not replace a sign language interpreter.
